CHALLENGE C0141 | Sorting by `i` (record index) natively provides chronological insertion order, which is the only reliable causal sequence in an append-only hash chain. Sorting by claimed `timestamp_utc` allows unsynchronized clocks or malicious actors to arbitrarily reorder the provenance trace, breaking the causal integrity of the evidence layer.

DESCRIPTION: FIND — In `_EvidenceIndex.__init__`, records are conditionally excluded from the in-memory index maps based on truthiness or positivity checks (`if rec.experiment:`, `if rec.model:`, `if rec.round_idx >= 0:`). Consequently, valid chain records that legitimately lack these metadata fields (e.g., experiment-wide health scans or global policy snapshots) are never indexed for those dimensions.
FOLLOW: Any downstream `EvidenceStore.query()` or `export_bundle()` call that explicitly attempts to filter for unassociated records (e.g., `query(model="")` or `query(round_idx=-1)`) will silently fail, intersecting with an empty set and returning zero results despite the records existing in the chain. This degraded completeness prevents auditing of non-model-specific artifacts.
